(going forward, I'm going to post all announcements about new toolchain releases in this topic)

EDIT: now that we have a separate channel for Lean releases, I will go back to one topic per release

We have a new stable release of Lean v4.24.0 and a new release candidate: v4.25.0-rc2.

Please see the release notes for v4.24.0 and v4.25.0 for full details.

As usual Mathlib, doc-gen4, verso, Batteries, Aesop, Cslib, and the REPL are available using these toolchains via the v4.24.0 and v4.25.0-rc2 tags at the respective repositories (and ProofWidgets at v0.0.75 / v0.078). We encourage all projects downstream of these to update when possible (and to release their own corresponding toolchain tags after updating). (Recall that you can use the lean-update github action to help automate this process.)

Notable this month with the release of v4.25.0-rc2 is the availability of the new module system (which must be activated using the experimental.module option in your lakefile). All repositories upstream of Mathlib (but not yet including Mathlib) have now been migrated to the module system. (Although much work remains to be done to fully utilize it, reducing imports and visibility.)

This is just a quick notice that users who depend on mathlib may want to hold off on upgrading to v4.25.0-rc2 for a bit. There are some issues with mathlib's cache on that version at the moment so mathlib has downgraded to v4.24.0 for the time being.

Mathlib, the REPL, and Cslib have now been updated, and the v4.25.0-rc2 tags have been replaced. As far as I can tell, it should now be safe to update downstream packages to use these versions. Thanks @Mario Carneiro, @Mac Malone, @Bryan Gin-ge Chen and @Sebastian Ullrich for help fixing this cache problem.

Notable this month with the release of v4.26.0-rc1 is that Mathlib has moved to the module system. I'll defer further discussion of this to the threads, but just leave you with this as a teaser of what is now possible:

Fast rebuilds!
(discussion of using the new module system at #mathlib4 > Mathlib has moved to the new module system @ 💬)

We have released toolchains v4.24.1 and v4.25.2, containing a bugfix (lean#11328) for a significant memory leak.

There are corresponding v4.24.1 and v4.25.2 tags for Mathlib available (although not other repositories: contact me if you need these).

If you are planning on continuing to use the v4.24 and v4.25 stable releases, I would advise switching to these toolchains.

There will be a new release candidate for v4.26, but we are a preparing a few others things to go in before cutting that.

This memory leak has been present since v4.18. If you are still using v4.18 through v4.23 and think you may be significantly affected by a memory leak, please contact me to discuss your use case.

We have a new stable release of Lean v4.26.0 and a new release candidate: v4.27.0-rc1.

Please see the release notes for v4.26.0 and v4.27.0 for full details.

As usual Mathlib, doc-gen4, verso, Batteries, Aesop, Cslib, and the REPL are available using these toolchains via the v4.26.0 and v4.27.0-rc1 tags at the respective repositories (and ProofWidgets at v0.0.83 / v0.084). We encourage all projects downstream of these to update when possible (and to release their own corresponding toolchain tags after updating). (Recall that you can use the lean-update github action to help automate this process.)

This release completes the revision of the String API, including dependently typed String.Pos, full API support for String.Slice, and iterators using the new Iterator API. There are also many additions to the TreeMap/HashMap API, including intersection, difference, and BEq. And many changes to grind which I will discuss elsewhere.
(placeholder for missing announcement for Lean versions v4.27.0 and v4.28.0-rc1 last month; sorry)

We have a new stable release of Lean v4.28.0 and a new release candidate: v4.29.0-rc1.

Please see the release notes for v4.28.0 and v4.29.0 for full details.

As usual Mathlib, doc-gen4, verso, Batteries, Aesop, Cslib, and the REPL are available using these toolchains via the v4.28.0 and v4.29.0-rc1 tags at the respective repositories (and ProofWidgets at v0.0.87 / v0.088).

We encourage all projects downstream to update to v4.28.0 when possible (and to release their own corresponding toolchain tags after updating). (Recall that you can use the lean-update github action to help automate this process.)

However: unlike most months we do not yet advise downstream projects to move to v4.29.0-rc1, which is more of a :construction_zone: release candidate :construction_zone: than usual, and we will certainly be making further release candidates in this series before reaching a stable version.

Projects which would like to move to v4.29.0-rc1 despite this advice may consider adding set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false as either a global option in their lakefile, or wherever needed. We anticipate the need for this option will be reduced by subsequent release candidates.

v4.29.0-rc1 bring fixes to two long-standing problems in Lean, via lean#12286 and particularly lean#12179. Downstream projects, particularly Mathlib, have over the years taken advantage of the previous treatment of reducibility settings in core Lean algorithms, and during the release candidate process we will be iterating with Mathlib --- both to fix problems in Mathlib, and identify further follow-up changes in Lean.

Due to the size of Mathlib, and the sheer number of interactions with these changes in Lean, we decided that it was not possible to resolve all the issues through our nightly-testing branches. Hence we've deployed v4.29.0-rc1 with a large number of occurrences of set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in Mathlib. Some of these are the result of problems in Mathlib, other will need minimized test cases that we can address in followup release candidates. (Both processes have already started.) All users of v4.29.0-rc1, and in particular Mathlib users, are invited to participate constructively in this process! :-)

For Mathlib contributors who don't want to know about these issues, we advise adding set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false at the top of new files being PR'd, or on individual declarations when refactoring existing files, and we will clean these up later.

The underlying changes in v4.29.0-rc1 result in more predictable behaviour and better performance. We're happy to delay the timing of our release schedule to make sure that the stable release of v4.29.0 is a great experience for all users.
Please continue discussion specific to Mathlib on v4.29.0-rc1 in #mathlib4 > Adapting Mathlib to `v4.29.0-rc1` @ 💬
v4.28.1 has been released, with a fix for lean4#13388.
